teaching.hint: Does arriving at a mirror from the left allow the same continuation as arriving from above?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: A mirror's next direction depends on its incoming direction, so a cell needs separate counts for rightward and downward arrivals. Every transition still increases row plus column.
solution_outline.approach: Count walks through cells by their arrival direction. From an empty cell, send all arriving paths right and down; from a mirror, send rightward arrivals down and downward arrivals right. Skip transitions beyond the grid and sum both arrival counts at the destination.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: For each processed cell, its two counts equal the numbers of valid partial walks that reach it from the left and from above. Mirrors are passed through with a forced turn, so these states include reflection chains without separately simulating them.
solution_outline.correctness: Every partial path has a unique previous cell and incoming direction. The transition for that previous cell sends it to exactly the legal next state, including a mirror's forced turn; off-grid transitions are discarded. Row-plus-column strictly increases, so processing in grid order counts each path once and the destination sum is exact.
solution_outline.complexity: O(mn) time and O(mn) auxiliary space for the two direction counts at each cell; counts are reduced modulo 10^9+7.
solution_outline.pitfall: A single count per mirror loses the arrival direction and can send a path along the wrong reflected continuation.

accepted_alternatives: Rolling rows can keep the same two directional states in O(n) auxiliary space while retaining O(mn) time.
common_wrong_turns: Allow a new choice at every mirror
Follow a reflection that exits the grid
Merge the two arrival directions into one state
source_fidelity_notes: The source's long path diagrams were replaced by compact grid cases; before-entry chained reflections, forced turn directions, invalid exits, endpoint emptiness, bounds, and modulus were retained.
